answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Matching. Each agent publishes a per-epoch behavioural fingerprint (action-mix vector). Admission requires the current epoch's vector to lie within a bounded divergence of the agent's own trailing median; a fresh identity has no history, so its first epochs sit at the population-median plume, offering no nectar (fee rebates, routing priority) until consistency accrues toward a verified zenith. Attackers must run each clone through many full epochs of coherent behaviour before payoffs unlock, multiplying time and idle compute per fake identity.
